server.registry_source: GET /health -> tools_status (live map of endpoint names to availability)
server.registry_refresh_hint: If a tool 404s, re-fetch /health and reload this manifest's tool_registry; endpoints are the registry keys, not friendly names.

response_shape.success_is: boolean, true when the tool ran (NOT when findings are confirmed)
response_shape.note: success=true only means the binary ran. Always parse stdout and run verification before believing any claim.

safety_policy.SAFE: Read-only reconnaissance. Runs without confirmation on the local host or targets in config/hexstrike_scope.json.
safety_policy.REVIEW: Intrusive or state-changing. Requires confirmed=true for that exact call.
safety_policy.DANGER: Exploitation, credential cracking, traffic poisoning or MITM. MARK LIII refuses to run these and explains why instead.
rule_order: DANGER is refused before any other check.
Local host (loopback, own hostname, own IPs) is always allowed for SAFE tools.
Targets in hexstrike_scope.json allowed_targets pass for SAFE and REVIEW (REVIEW still needs confirmed=true).
Everything else is refused with an explanation of how to authorise it.

tool_registry.note: Installable tools will 404 or fail until their binaries are installed on the server host. Check availability before promising a result.

nmap.args_hint: scan_type like -sV (version) or -sC (scripts) or -sS (syn); ports like 1-1000 or 80,443
nmap.when_to_use: First step for any host: find open ports and service versions.
nmap.output_notes: Parse lines like '9999/tcp open http Werkzeug httpd 3.1.8'. 'Not shown: N closed tcp ports' means the rest are closed.
nmap.verify_how: TCP-connect every claimed open port; HTTP ports get a curl status probe.
nmap.false_positive_notes: Version strings can be guesses when a service sends no banner; default-page HTTP responses make banners unreliable.

nuclei.args_hint: target as URL; severity as critical,high,medium,low,info filter
nuclei.when_to_use: Template-driven CVE and misconfiguration scanning of a live web target.
nuclei.verify_how: curl the exact finding URL; 404/410 refutes, 200/401/403 keeps it alive.
nuclei.false_positive_notes: Error-page text matching is common; always re-request the exact path.

gobuster.args_hint: url REQUIRED (server 400s without it); mode dir|dns|vhost|fuzz
gobuster.when_to_use: Discover hidden directories, vhosts or DNS names on a web target.
gobuster.verify_how: curl each discovered path; treat 404 now as refuted.
gobuster.false_positive_notes: Soft-404 pages return 200 for everything; check body uniqueness.

dirb.when_to_use: Alternative directory brute force with recursion.

dirsearch.when_to_use: Threaded path discovery with extension fuzzing.

feroxbuster.when_to_use: Fast rust content discovery with recursion.

ffuf.when_to_use: Fuzzing anything in a request: paths, params, headers, subdomains.

wfuzz.when_to_use: Classic payload fuzzing when ffuf is unavailable.

httpx.when_to_use: Quick liveness/title/tech probing of many hosts or host:port pairs.
httpx.output_notes: One line per live host with status code and title.
httpx.verify_how: curl one representative host to confirm liveness pattern.

wafw00f.when_to_use: Identify a WAF before aggressive scanning so you can slow down.

nikto.when_to_use: Deep web server config assessment; loud and slow but thorough.
nikto.output_notes: OSVDB entries and '+ /dir/: directory indexing found' style lines.
nikto.verify_how: curl each claimed path or behaviour.
nikto.false_positive_notes: Nikto flags many informational items; classify before alarming the user.

wpscan.when_to_use: WordPress core/plugin/theme/user enumeration with vulnerability DB.
wpscan.verify_how: curl the wp-content paths it claims exist.

sqlmap.when_to_use: Never. Actively exploits SQL injection and modifies target data.
sqlmap.output_notes: MARK LIII refuses; suggest read-only confirmation of the injection point with curl tests instead.

arjun.when_to_use: Find hidden HTTP parameters an endpoint accepts.
arjun.verify_how: Send one request with the parameter and compare response size.

paramspider.when_to_use: Mine archived URLs and parameters for a domain.

hakrawler.when_to_use: Spider JS and links to enumerate endpoints quickly.

zaproxy.when_to_use: Full active web scan via OWASP ZAP; intrusive.

burpsuite.when_to_use: Headless Burp scan when configured on the server.

subfinder.when_to_use: Passive subdomain enumeration; no packets touch the target.
subfinder.verify_how: Resolve a sample of subdomains; report resolution rate.
subfinder.false_positive_notes: Passive sources go stale; unresolved hosts may be historical.

amass.when_to_use: Thorough attack-surface mapping when subfinder is too shallow.

dnsenum.when_to_use: DNS records, brute subdomains and zone-transfer attempts.

fierce.when_to_use: Quick DNS recon focused on subdomain takeover candidates.

theharvester.when_to_use: Harvest emails, names and hosts from public sources.

sherlock.when_to_use: Find a username's accounts across social platforms.
sherlock.false_positive_notes: Platform pages that always 200 inflate hits; verify profiles show the username.

spiderfoot.when_to_use: Aggregate OSINT across dozens of sources when configured.

maltego.when_to_use: Graph-based OSINT transforms when the server has it configured.

social-analyzer.when_to_use: Deep profile analysis for a username or name.

searchsploit.when_to_use: After fingerprinting a service version: find public exploits offline.
searchsploit.verify_how: Report only; do not run the exploit.

msfconsole.when_to_use: Only for read-only 'search' queries when the plugin whitelist allows; module execution is refused.

responder.when_to_use: Never. Poisons name services to capture hashes.

evil-winrm.when_to_use: Never. Interactive shell on a remote host.

nxc.when_to_use: With confirmed=true for enumeration flags only (e.g. --shares, --users); credential validation is refused.
nxc.args_hint: protocol smb|ssh|winrm|ldap; add module-less enumeration flags only
nxc.verify_how: Re-run read-only enumeration flags manually if the result matters.

smbmap.when_to_use: List SMB share permissions on a Windows/Samba host.

enum4linux-ng.when_to_use: Rich SMB/Windows enumeration: users, groups, policy, shares.

enum4linux.when_to_use: Legacy fallback when enum4linux-ng is unavailable.

rpcclient.when_to_use: Raw RPC queries against Windows hosts.

nbtscan.when_to_use: NetBIOS name scan of a subnet.

arp-scan.when_to_use: Layer-2 host discovery on the local segment.
arp-scan.verify_how: Cross-check MAC vendors; single-ARP replies are reliable.

masscan.when_to_use: With confirmed=true and a low rate on your own large networks.
masscan.false_positive_notes: Masscan can lie about open ports on lossy links; re-verify with nmap.

autorecon.when_to_use: One-command full enumeration sweep with confirmed=true.
autorecon.output_notes: Results land under the server's output dir; stdout summarises.

verified_params.requires: username or username_file AND password or password_file

hydra.when_to_use: Never from MARK LIII. Lockouts, account noise, and its results are the classic false positive (wins against servers with no auth).
hydra.output_notes: If a user asks for hydra anyway, explain the safety policy and offer an authorised offline audit instead.
hydra.false_positive_notes: http-get against an unauthenticated server reports the FIRST password as valid. Verify any credential claim with bare/good/bad curl status comparison.

john.when_to_use: Never offline-cracks on request; but hash-identifier is the SAFE alternative for identifying a hash.

hash-identifier.when_to_use: Identify an unknown hash's algorithm; read-only and instant.

trivy.args_hint: scan_type image|fs|repo|config; target is image name or path
trivy.when_to_use: Container image and filesystem vulnerability scanning; your own images only.
trivy.output_notes: CVE ID, package, installed and fixed versions.
trivy.verify_how: Spot-check one CVE against the upstream advisory.

checksec.when_to_use: Binary hardening: NX, PIE, canary, RELRO status.

binwalk.when_to_use: Find embedded files and firmware signatures in a binary or image.

foremost.when_to_use: Carve files out of disk images or dumps.

strings.when_to_use: Quick readable-string extraction from any binary.

file.when_to_use: Identify a file's true type before deeper analysis.

radare2.when_to_use: Static disassembly and quick function inventory.

objdump.when_to_use: Disassemble object files; check sections and symbols.

ropper.when_to_use: ROP gadget listing for binary analysis on your own samples.

tcpdump.args_hint: cap with -c 200 or -a duration style limits so it self-terminates
tcpdump.when_to_use: Packet capture on your own interfaces with confirmed=true.

tshark.when_to_use: Structured packet analysis on your own network.

wireshark.when_to_use: GUI alternative; prefer tshark headless on a server.

kismet.when_to_use: Wireless network discovery on your own spectrum.

airmon-ng.when_to_use: Enable monitor mode on YOUR OWN wifi adapter with confirmed=true.

aireplay-ng.when_to_use: Never. Injects frames into live networks.

curl.when_to_use: Direct HTTP probing; the verifier's own backbone.

httpie.when_to_use: Friendly HTTP requests when curl formatting is awkward.

dotdotpwn.when_to_use: Path traversal probing with confirmed=true on authorised targets.

steghide.when_to_use: Steganography extraction from your own images.

rustscan.when_to_use: Faster port discovery feeding nmap; install rustscan then re-check /health.
rustscan.install_hint: cargo install rustscan or apt install rustscan

shodan-cli.when_to_use: External exposure lookups once installed and API key set.

censys-cli.when_to_use: Certificate and host metadata search once installed.

ghidra.install_hint: install ghidra and expose analyzeHeadless on PATH

clair.when_to_use: Container static analysis once a clair server exists.
clair.install_hint: deploy clair server, then connect the tool

pwntools.when_to_use: Never from MARK LIII; exploit development framework.

metasploit.install_hint: use msfconsole (already available) rather than installing a second copy

quick_host_scan.description: Answer 'is this host open and what runs on it' in under a minute.

steps.report: one line per port: verdict, service, version confidence

deep_host_scan.description: Full assessment of one host you are authorised to test.

steps.only_if: an http port is open and target is authorised

steps.report: grouped by port; verified vs unverifiable vs refuted

web_app_scan.description: Web application triage on an authorised URL.

steps.verify: curl each discovered path and each finding

steps.report: WAF status, live endpoints, verified findings only

osint_domain.description: Passive intelligence on a domain without touching its servers.

steps.report: subdomain count, resolved rate, notable records, email list

container_audit.description: Audit one of your own container images.

steps.verify: spot-check the top CVE against upstream advisories

steps.report: critical and high CVEs with fix versions

binary_triage.description: First look at an unknown binary sample.

steps.report: type, protections, notable strings, embedded artifacts

false_positive_hints: hydra/medusa/patator 'valid password found' is a false positive when the service has no authentication: verify by comparing HTTP status with no creds, the claimed creds, and wrong creds; identical statuses refute the claim.
nmap version strings are guesses when banners are absent or a default page answers; label them low-confidence unless a second source agrees.
directory scanners get soft-404s: a 200 with a generic error body is not a real page; verify body content.
nuclei matches error-page text on some templates: re-request the exact path before reporting.
masscan reports open on lossy links; confirm each port with nmap or a TCP connect.
passive OSINT (subfinder, sherlock) mixes stale and spoofed entries; resolve or load a sample before reporting.
subdomain takeovers need a CNAME plus an unregistered upstream; a dangling CNAME alone is not a takeover.
always distinguish 'tool ran successfully' (success=true) from 'finding confirmed' (verification verdict).

parameter_map.description: How MARK LIII's flat plugin parameters map onto server payloads

required_param_checks.gobuster: url is required; server returns 400 'URL parameter is required' without it
required_param_checks.hydra: username or username_file AND password or password_file are both required; server 400s otherwise
required_param_checks.nmap: target is required; scan_type defaults to -sV

jarvis_usage_guide.mission: Give MARK LIII a complete, safe, self-verifying cybersecurity arm powered by the HexStrike MCP server on port 9999.
before_anything: Load this manifest once per session; it is the source of truth for endpoint names and availability.
Check GET /health; classify the server as healthy (77+ tools) or degraded (some missing).
If /health is unreachable, use the plugin's self-diagnosis: not_installed, not_running, or port_changed, each with its remedy.
choosing_a_tool: Recon first, always: nmap for hosts, subfinder/dnsenum for domains, httpx for liveness.
Fingerprint before vuln-scanning: use service+version from nmap to choose nuclei tags or searchsploit queries.
Prefer SAFE tools; escalate to REVIEW only with a purpose; never run DANGER tools.
If a chosen tool is not in tool_registry.available, say it is missing and offer the install_hint instead of failing mysteriously.
running_a_tool: POST to /api/tools/<endpoint> with a JSON body; map plugin params per parameter_map.
Treat success=true as 'the binary ran', never as 'a finding is confirmed'.
Cache identical calls for two minutes; do not re-run identical scans inside a conversation turn.
verification_contract: Every open port claim gets a TCP connect re-test.
Every HTTP service claim gets a curl status probe; default pages downgrade confidence.
Every credential claim gets the three-way status comparison; identical statuses mean refuted.
Every web finding gets a re-request of the exact URL; 404/410 refutes.
Every version claim needs a second source to be called confirmed.
reporting_style: Group results by target and port.
Stamp each finding: VERIFIED, UNVERIFIABLE, or REFUTED, with one-line evidence.
Lead with verified facts; keep refuted noise in a single summary line.
State tool runtime and whether the scan was cached.
Never speak a refuted finding as fact; that is the whole point of the verifier.
safety_and_ethics: Scan only the local host or targets in config/hexstrike_scope.json.
Adding a remote target needs the user's explicit confirmation on the HUD.
REVIEW tools additionally need confirmed=true on the specific call.
DANGER tools are refused with an explanation; offer the SAFE alternative instead.
If asked to attack a third party, refuse and explain the policy.
debugging_itself: HTTP 404 from the API means the endpoint name is wrong: reload tools_status from /health and re-resolve via endpoint_aliases.
HTTP 400 means a required parameter is missing: check required_param_checks.
Connection refused means the server is down: offer the open_server action.
return_code != 0 with 'command not found' in stderr means the binary is missing server-side: offer install_hint.
Timeouts mean the scan was too broad: narrow ports, wordlists, or severity and retry.
Never retry a failed call more than twice; diagnose instead.
speed_rules: Use the plugin's result cache; identical calls within 120s return instantly.
Run quick_scan before deep_scan; deep_scan reuses quick_scan results.
Batch OSINT tools together; they are passive and fast.
Skip nuclei when no HTTP port is open.
For big sweeps, prefer autorecon with confirmed=true rather than chaining a dozen calls.

answer_patterns.how_many_tools: Read total_tools_count and total_tools_available from /health; today: 127 registered, 77 available, 47 installable.
answer_patterns.what_can_you_do: Summarise playbooks and the SAFE/REVIEW/DANGER split, not the raw tool list.
answer_patterns.found_something: Report verdict-stamped findings with evidence, and offer the next playbook step.

download_optimization.problem: This network throttles github.com archive and release downloads to single-digit bytes per second while other routes run at full speed (measured 2026-09-19: codeload 975 KB/s vs github.com archive 0 B/s).
download_optimization.rule: Never download from github.com/<owner>/<repo>/archive/... or github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/... URLs.

fast_routes.release_asset: Query https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases/latest for the asset's browser_download_url, then download that URL
fast_routes.pypi_packages: https://pypi.org is unthrottled; prefer pip installs
fast_routes.go_tools: proxy.golang.org is unthrottled; go install works normally

download_optimization.proven_result: projectdiscovery/nuclei-templates main tarball (9.8 MB) downloaded via codeload in ~12 s at 850 KB/s after the archive route stalled.

local_setup_done.nuclei_templates: $HOME/nuclei-templates (13,755 yaml templates, updated 2026-09-19) — resolve $HOME, never hardcode a user path
local_setup_done.nuclei_config: ~/.config/nuclei/config.yaml pins templates-directory and disables update checks
local_setup_done.note: First nuclei run builds a template index and can take minutes; later runs are fast. Do not point Jarvis at nuclei before the index exists.
local_setup_done.fixed_permissions: ~/.config/nuclei, ~/.config/uncover and ~/.config/subfinder were root-owned and had to be chowned back to the user

download_optimization.update_procedure: To refresh templates later: curl -sL https://codeload.github.com/projectdiscovery/nuclei-templates/tar.gz/refs/heads/main -o /tmp/nt.tgz && tar -xzf /tmp/nt.tgz -C /tmp && rsync -a --delete /tmp/nuclei-templates-main/ "$HOME/nuclei-templates/"

local_fast_lane.description: plugins/hexstrike_mcp.py runs allowlisted binaries directly via core/local_exec.py when installed locally — same safety gate, same verifier, no HTTP hop to port 9999.
local_fast_lane.fallback: When a binary is missing locally, the call goes to the HexStrike server instead.
local_fast_lane.benefit: Sub-second scans for local targets and the security stack keeps working even when the server is down.

scan_speed_policy.why_this_exists: A slow scan looks like a network problem but almost never is. The 'Speed: 4 B/s' bar in the HUD is computed as output bytes divided by elapsed seconds, so it measures how QUIET a command is, not how fast the network is. A tarpitting host produces almost no output while nmap waits, which drives the number toward single digits for minutes.
scan_speed_policy.root_cause: nmap service-version probing (-sV) against routers, IoT and embedded devices. Those boxes accept the TCP connection and then never answer the probe, so nmap idles against --host-timeout. Measured on the local gateway: nmap -sV took 65s and found nothing; the same scan without -sV took 1.4s and found every port.
hard_rules: Never request -sV for discovery. Discover ports first, then identify services with 2-second socket banner reads.
Every nmap invocation carries --max-retries 1 --host-timeout 25s --open, on both the local and the server lane.
If -sV is genuinely needed, run it only against ports already known to be open, with --version-intensity 2.
Every pipeline stage has a wall-clock budget (discovery 30s, version probe 40s, httpx 45s, nuclei 45s). A stalled stage is cut off and reported, never silently retried.
Prefer the local fast lane: allowlisted binaries run directly with no HTTP hop, and they work when the HexStrike server is down.

measured.local_gateway_quick_pipeline_after: 6.5s including independent verification of every port

scan_speed_policy.binary_flavour_guard: httpx on PATH is the Python HTTP client, not ProjectDiscovery's prober. The plugin checks the binary flavour and refuses to dispatch the wrong one; install ProjectDiscovery's as httpx-toolkit.
how_jarvis_should_talk_about_it: Report wall-clock seconds from the stage timer, never the HUD byte bar.
If a stage was cut off by its budget, say so and keep the confirmed findings.
Never present a version string from a tarpitted probe as fact; banner-verified strings only.

registry_corrections.why: tool_registry.installable is the HexStrike server's own 'what I would install / believe is missing' view. It is NOT a presence check. Verified on this host 2026-09-19: 0 of its 47 names resolve to a binary of that exact name, and several of those tools are already installed under a different name. Never tell the user to install something on that list before checking the mapping below.

misleading_names.metasploit: Already installed. Use msfconsole (interactive) or msfvenom (payloads).
misleading_names.sleuthkit: Already installed, and it is a suite not a single binary: fls, icat, mmls, istat, tsk_recover.
misleading_names.exploit-db: Already installed. The command-line front end is searchsploit.
misleading_names.ropgadget: Already installed. The binary name is capitalised: ROPgadget.
misleading_names.pwntools: Already installed as a Python module, not a binary: python3 -m pwn / python3 -c 'import pwn'.
misleading_names.shodan-cli: Already installed as 'shodan'. Run 'shodan init <api-key>' once before any query.
misleading_names.censys-cli: Already installed as 'censys'. Requires API credentials before any query.

not_local_clis.hashcat-utils: A suite of separate helper binaries; there is no 'hashcat-utils' command to call.
not_local_clis.libc-database: A git-cloned data directory used by other scripts, not an executable.
not_local_clis.have-i-been-pwned: A web API, not a local tool. Needs an API key; h8mail is the local client for it.
not_local_clis.stegsolve: A Java GUI jar; unusable from a non-interactive lane.
not_local_clis.api-schema-analyzer: Not a real local tool. Do not present it as installed or installable.
not_local_clis.graphql-scanner: Not a real local tool. For GraphQL use the HexStrike endpoint, or curl/httpx against the endpoint.
not_local_clis.jwt-analyzer: Not a real local tool. Use the jwt-tool actions in this checkout, or the Python jwt library.

registry_corrections.rule: Before advising any install, resolve the corrected name through the local fast lane first. If the corrected name answers, the capability is already present and you should say so rather than proposing an install.

schema_note: This file is read by plugins/hexstrike_mcp.py. Keep it valid JSON; the plugin degrades gracefully to its built-in catalogue if the file is unreadable.
